summary: Specific cross-school and overlapping student-file grants were repaired and regression-tested. The overall ruleset is not ready for real school data: same-school confidential records remain broadly readable, capability boundaries and schemas are incomplete, and live client operations do not match server-only write rules. This score applies to the remaining full ruleset, not only the repaired paths.

findings.issue: All authenticated users of a school can read complaints, messages, leaves, notifications and user profiles without recipient, participant or subject relationship checks. School membership alone does not authorize access to another child's medical leave, complaint or private conversation.
findings.recommendation: Separate public directory fields from private profiles. Enforce owner/participant/recipient relationships and specific staff capabilities. Add same-school unrelated-user denial tests and query-level tests.

findings.issue: Generic isStaff grants are reused across academic, financial and operational collections; librarians and transport roles can receive powers unrelated to their duties. Parent/student creates do not consistently bind sender, applicant or student IDs to the authenticated relationship.
findings.recommendation: Define domain capabilities, teacher class/subject assignments and immutable actor/owner fields. Derive actor and school server-side and validate linked student ownership.

findings.issue: The Android Firebase datasource directly writes sensitive student, teacher, fee, attendance and report-card records that the rules intentionally deny. It uses reportCards while the canonical rule path is report_cards. Broad collection listeners for parents/students are also incompatible with relationship-scoped reads; rules do not filter unauthorized rows out of a collection query.
findings.recommendation: Implement authenticated server commands and scoped read queries. Standardize collection, school and session identifiers. Surface permission/write errors instead of retaining sample data.

findings.issue: Most writable collections have no field allowlist or immutable ownership/session constraints on updates, beyond matching the resulting school/session. A permitted staff writer can replace unrelated fields or rewrite an existing document's relationship fields.
findings.recommendation: Use separate create/update schemas, affectedKeys allowlists, immutable relationships, and server-validated domain transitions. Test valid create followed by malicious update and merge operations.

findings.issue: Firestore creates and updates generally lack field type validation, required/allowed keys, timestamp checks, score bounds and constrained enum values. Role checks alone cannot preserve record integrity.
findings.recommendation: Validate complete domain schemas at the server boundary and add compatible rule constraints for any remaining direct client writes. Reject unknown keys, invalid types and invalid transitions.

findings.issue: Firestore document creation has no application-level string/array limits or per-actor quotas. Storage has a per-file size/MIME restriction but no per-school/user file quota or content verification. Platform maximums do not prevent cost or resource abuse.
findings.recommendation: Bound text, arrays, bulk operations and file counts; enforce quotas on server-mediated writes, add budget alerts and use an upload validation/quarantine flow where required.

findings.issue: The repaired students namespace enforces self/linked-parent access, including a student ID claim distinct from Firebase UID. However, every other category is still readable by the entire school. Confidential checked papers, financial exports or staff files must not be stored in that broad namespace.
findings.recommendation: Allowlist truly shared material categories and create separately scoped private file paths. Inventory actual upload destinations and avoid distributing persistent public download tokens for sensitive files.

findings.issue: The HTTP bootstrap routes now require verified administrator claims. Initial trusted administrator provisioning, claim revocation policy, full query access, historical sessions and same-school privacy still need acceptance tests. Existing passing tests cover a bounded subset rather than certify the whole policy.
findings.recommendation: Use a trusted operator bootstrap procedure and maintain a role/capability/tenant/session/ownership test matrix. Deploy only after app query/command contracts pass emulator and staging checks.
